text: In nineteen fourteen, nations agreed the first international treaty for the Safety of Life at Sea. Lifeboat space for everyone on board. Radios staffed day and night. And an International Ice Patrol, which still watches the North Atlantic for icebergs today. Later ships got double hulls and taller watertight walls, so a long scrape can't flood them the same way. The Titanic wasn't sunk by one big failure. It was a chain of small ones, lined up in the dark. Which link in that chain do you think mattered most? Tell me in the comments.
